by: Claude Opus 5.5 design panel (three proposals, three judges, synthesis)
decision:
M3's next step is a measurement step that changes nothing in the live chat, the index or the profile. It takes the checked-relations plan (ranked first by two of three judges) as the frame and adds the best parts of the other two.

WHAT THE STEP DOES
- Tests roadmap question 1 (do right relations bring the deciding provision into the context) with at most 40 relations whose correctness can be checked in the act's own words. They are laid over the experiment runner's bundles; nothing is ingested.
- Tests roadmap question 2 (is automatic extraction accurate enough) against a provision-level gold set built from the act with no model, with bars fixed before any run.
- Writes the second hard catalogue S1.0 asks for: 15 questions, the first with other-act and municipal cases, frozen before the relation file exists.
- Cost: under 0.10 USD at plan prices, in two paid runs.

ARMS (answer-free, no rerank, date 2026-10-15)
- A base, C model cards, D the act's own cross-references: as in ADR-057.
- L: the live chat profile v3 itself. It splits card additions from cross-references in the shared 13 places for the first time.
- F: arm C's room (4 more passages, 3000 tokens) with the checked relations only.
- G: live v3 with the checked relations added to the model's cards.

HYPOTHESES AND STOP RULES
- Early stop: if L already finds the deciding phrase in 11 or more of the 13 non-control questions of the new catalogue, F and G are not built for the server run and the ADR records that search does not lose these shapes.
- H1: on the new catalogue F finds at least 10 of 13 and at least 4 more than D. Every F miss must carry a named reason. F on catalogues 1 and 2 (expected 14 of 15; measured A 8, C 10, D 12) is reported as a wiring test only, because the relations target those known misses.
- H3 (the decision): split F's gain over D by how the relation was warranted. If at least two thirds comes through relations read from the text (incoming, own-section, exact subsection, named other act), the next PR extends the reader and needs no cards. If under half, the card route and its verification are the real work.
- H4 (ceiling): one baseline run of the live chat on the questions where F beat D. If the chat already answers 80% or more, the work stops (ADR-054 rule: no measurable gain, keep the simpler variant).
- Bounds for any later product use: at most one in four of F's added passages outside the deciding provision; mean context at most 800 tokens above D.
- Extraction bars: 0 wrong targets in 60 sampled pointer links; at most 3 wrong (target, type or direction) and no reversed exception in the 76 cross-passage card pairs. Below that, a typed relation is never shown to the model.

DROPPED, AND WHY
- A live profile v4 with four structure rules in this step: largest production risk, no rollback named, and one rule depends on the unmeasured ADR-062 stage 2. The rules survive as warrant classes in the experiment and, if H3 holds, as a later reader extension, one rule per PR.
- "LasteKS § 27¹ cannot be reached by structure": wrong. I checked RT 111072026042: § 27¹ lg 1 says "käesoleva seaduse § 27 kohaselt", and it is the only mention of § 27 in the act. An incoming reference reaches it.
- An experiment arm inside lib/rag-v2/search/profiles.js and retrieval.js: it would collide with the uncommitted stage 2 changes to retrieval.js and deploy with the PR. The overlay in the runner script replaces it.
- The relations-only model pass and a catalogue v4 run in this step: moved to the follow-up set that waits for the owner.
- The hypothesis that G loses at least 2 questions F finds: nothing measured supports it. G stays as a reported arm.
- "Right by construction" for relation types: it holds for the pointer, not the type. Every text-derived relation gets one mechanical type, chosen only so the traversal follows it from both ends (QUALIFIES; reverse kinds are EXCEPTION_TO, DEFINES, QUALIFIES, SUPERSEDES). No typed relation reaches a model in this step.
- Two statements in the brief: the repo does not confirm v47 as live (S1.0 line 96 says production is corpus v46), and the card count is 780 in 7 files (761 without the Harku annex).

WHAT I VERIFIED IN C:\Users\rauds\AppData\Local\Temp\wt-dates (read-only, still 18 changed entries)
- Branch claude/rag-v2-provision-dates at 5ba1e4a1 with ADR-062 stage 2 uncommitted; its paid block is still "TÄITA PÄRAST JOOKSU".
- The reader has no handling of "käesoleva paragrahvi" pointers. Search adds the first passage of a referenced section (retrieval.js line 326), and card dependencies run before cross-references (lines 306 to 334).
- The overlay is feasible in the script alone: retrieve() reads postgres.retrievalDirectory (line 102) and postgres.bundles (116) and compares them at line 123, so the directory row must be recomputed; indexUnit (embedding.js line 60) does not read cards.
- Card files: 780 cards, 282 relations, 61 unresolved; no relation crosses a batch part in any file; SHS § 132 lg 7 has EXCEPTION_TO only in the 01.10 file (p7-c18 to p7-c7), none in the 12.06 file (p7-c5).
- Manifest: SHS 130062026065 is in force 01.10 to 30.11.2026; the four later SHS versions have no card file.
- The dialogue evaluator has --only and --dry-run and no date option.
- The 11 reader and experiment tests pass offline.
- Prices: 130, 125 and 500 nano-USD per token (scripts/rag-v2-pilot-plan.mjs line 48); catalogue v4 was 0.198 USD for 40 turns (ADR-048).

NOT VERIFIED: anything on the server, and the proposals' corpus-wide scratch counts (the files exist; the repo script in step 2 recounts them).

The worktree is not clean main; ADR-062 stage 2 is uncommitted there and changes retrieval.js. M3 starts after it merges, and the implementing-provision question is dropped if the active generation lacks reader v30 data.

No person verified any relation. 'Checked' means a warrant in the text plus two AI readers; the hand check is done by reading, not by a lawyer. The unnamed class is capped at 12 and reported apart until the owner or Codex has read the page.

The relation set is built for the sections the catalogues name, so F's hits measure whether a right relation reaches the context (roadmap question 1), not how much of the law is covered. Coverage is answered only by the gold set. Catalogues 1 and 2 are a wiring test, and both are already at the ceiling in the whole chat (9/9 and 6/6).

The answer-free measure is not answer quality, and the runner has no reranker and none of the chat's lanes (no national-law reserve). A region per question only puts municipal texts in scope. The baseline chat run may show the chat already answers these; then the work stops.

The overlay is not the production path. It says nothing about ingest, index size or re-anchoring. Cross-document targets are resolved at run time, while production needs version-pinned targets that break on every re-ingest; an act-identity and version resolver does not exist.

Edge order within a card is by ID hash and at most 4 passages are added, so with several relations on one provision F can miss for reasons unrelated to correctness. This is reported per miss; a fix would touch dependencies.js and belongs to a later PR.

The only in-force SHS card file is on RT 130062026065, valid to 30.11.2026; versions 111072026120 to 111072026123 are indexed without cards. On 01.12.2026 the live chat loses the SHS cards, including the § 132 lg 7 relation. A carry-forward by exact quote looks feasible (scratch: 231 of 244 quotes and 92 of 107 relations found verbatim) but is not part of this step and needs an owner decision before then.

Server dependencies: the 30.09 per-question files and stored evaluation turns may be gone (turns carry an expiry), and SSH port 22 timed out on 30.09. Steps 2 to 9 give results locally even if the server run slips; whether local ingest of every scoped act runs fully offline was shown in scratch only.
The dialogue evaluator has no frozen date. The catalogue-3 phrases hold for the versions in force 01.10 to 30.11.2026 (LasteKS and HMS to 31.12.2026); a chat run after that needs new phrases.

All prices are plan-price estimates; ADR-054 and ADR-057 record no per-run cost for the hard catalogues. The real figure is on the OpenAI dashboard.

The proposals' corpus-wide scratch counts (for example 9 of 273, 84 of 122, 13 of 179) were not rerun here; only the files' existence and the card totals were confirmed. The repo script of step 2 is the first reproducible count.

ADR-057's own text is inconsistent on one point (four § 72 lg 2 questions in the catalogue, 'kolmes' in the whole-chat result), and which three questions the base found is an inference. Both are settled only by the server's per-question file.

proposals.title: M3.1: checked relations as dependency context, measured without answers first (arm F), on three hard catalogues
proposals.summary:
The plan answers the roadmap's first question (do right relations bring the deciding provision into the context?) with at most 40 relations whose correctness can be checked from the act's own words. It costs under 0.09 USD and changes nothing in the live chat or index.

What I found that shapes it:
- **The three known misses of the cross-reference arm (D) are three different shapes.**
  - LasteKS § 27¹ names § 27 ("käesoleva seaduse § 27 kohaselt"), so it is an incoming reference that the existing reader already resolves.
  - SHS § 59 lg 3 says "Käesoleva paragrahvi lõike 1 punktis 3 nimetatud isikul"; the reader returns nothing for own-section references.
  - SHS § 132 lg 7 names nothing and nothing names § 132; only a semantic relation can carry it.
- **Most relations therefore need no human judge.** Outgoing, incoming, own-section and named other-act references are right by construction of the deterministic reader. Only the unnamed kind needs judgement, and I cap it at 12.
- **No reindexing is needed.** The experiment runner can overlay relations on the bundles it loads; `retrieve()` and the profiles stay untouched. Arm F is arm C's room (4 more passages, 3000 tokens) with checked relations only; arm G merges them with the model's cards.
- **Verification without a human:** a deterministic check of each relation's warrant in the text, then a blind second reading by a fresh agent with decoy pairs. The label is "machine-checked, two readers", never "verified"; Codex re-reads the table at review time.
- **Free by-product:** the first recall and precision numbers for the model's extracted relations (roadmap question 2).

Paid steps: one embeddings call (under 0.001 USD) and one full-chat baseline run of 8 to 14 turns (0.05 to 0.08 USD at plan prices), which runs only if arm F beats D on at least four questions.

Two things the brief states that the repo does not confirm: v47 as live (S1.0 says production is v46), and a clean main (the worktree is branch `claude/rag-v2-provision-dates` with ADR-062 stage 2 uncommitted). The plan starts after stage 2 merges.

One production risk outside the experiment: the SHS cards sit on the version in force only until 30.11.2026, and the later SHS versions in the index have no card file.
proposals.hypothesis:
All four parts are measured on the generation active when the run happens, date 2026-10-15, no rerank.

H1 (the mechanism works when the relations are right):
- Catalogues 1 and 2 (15 questions): arm F puts the deciding phrase in the evidence in at least 14. Measured so far: A 8, C 10, D 12.
- New catalogue 3 (12 non-control questions, frozen before any run): F finds at least 9 and at least 4 more than D.
- Refuted if F is at or below 12 of 15 on the old catalogues, or finds fewer than 8 or gains fewer than 4 over D on catalogue 3.
- Every F miss must carry a named reason in the report (topic passage not among the nine seeds, `dependency_addition_limit`, `dependency_seed_limit`, `dependency_context_limit`); an unexplained miss also refutes it.

H2 (complete relations meet the caps): a card's edges are followed in edge-ID order and only 4 passages may be added. I expect arm G (model cards and checked relations together) to lose at least 2 questions that F finds. Refuted if G equals F; then no query-ordered traversal is needed.

H3 (which mechanism the product needs): of the questions F finds and D does not, at least two thirds come through reader-derived relations (incoming, own-section, named other act). Then the next product step is a reader extension with no cards. Refuted if fewer than half do; then relations need the card route and verification at scale is the real problem.

H4 (does the product miss them at all): in one full-chat run with the live profile v3, the chat misses at least half of the questions where F beat D. Refuted if v3 with plan and rerank already answers 80 % or more. That would be the ceiling effect of ADR-054 again; the relation layer then brings no measurable gain and the work stops, by the roadmap's own rule.

proposals.title: M3 step: measure relation extraction against a provision-level gold set, then switch on only what passes
proposals.summary:
Answer the roadmap's second question with numbers before buying or building anything: how accurate is each way of extracting relations, measured against links the act itself states.

Gold set (built from the act, no model):
- Unit: one provision (lõige). The Sotsiaalhoolekande seadus in force (RT 130062026065) has 855.
- Pointer links: every place where one provision names another, either in another section ("käesoleva seaduse § 72 lõikes 2") or in its own ("käesoleva paragrahvi lõikes 1"). SHS: 277 + 157 links, of which 273 + 40 lead to a different passage.
- Exception flag: an exception phrase in the same sentence (välja arvatud, erandina, ei kohaldata, erinevalt, arvestamata). SHS: 33 + 7 links.
- Negatives: provisions that deny a right and have no pointer in or out (the § 132 lg 7 shape). SHS: 18 by a crude pattern.
- The pointer links come from the same reader that is one of the extractors, so they count as gold only after a hand check of a fixed sample, stored with a review state outside the index.

What I already measured in scratch this session (free, local ingest with reader v30):
- Card relations (ADR-054) cover 9 of 273 pointer links to another section (3%), 4 of 40 own-section links (10%) and 7 of 18 negatives (39%).
- 84 of the 122 SHS card relation pairs (69%) join two cards in the same passage, so they cannot add a passage. Over the four in-force card documents 76 pairs cross passages; that is the whole set to hand-check.
- The live reader resolves 261 of 268 own references in SHS (97%). Search then adds the section's first passage: 13 of 179 pointers that name a lõige land in the wrong passage (7%), and it reads none of the own-section pointers.
- Whole index (519 acts, 13 669 passages): 2757 own references, 147 unresolved with a reason, 1840 other-act lists; 103 of 1496 lõige pointers fall outside the first passage; 329 of 1965 own-section pointers lead to another passage.

Proposed bars for switching on:
1. Untyped pointer that only adds the named passage: 0 wrong targets in 60 sampled links (true error then under 5% at 95% confidence) and at least 95% of gold links landing in the right passage.
2. Typed relation shown to the model as exception or condition: at most 3 wrong (target, type or direction) in the 76 cross-passage card pairs and no reversed exception; at most 2 wrong in the 40 exception-phrase links. Below that it stays an untyped "viitab" pointer.
3. Model extraction for more acts: only for what the reader cannot reach. Recall of at least 0.5 on the negatives (now 7 of 18), bar 2 met, and a search gain on negative-shaped questions. Extending cards to the 519 legal acts would cost about 4 USD at plan price (my estimate from 0.16 USD per 27 parts).

Paid work comes last and is gated: at most four runs, about 0.34 USD at plan price, announced as a set before it starts.
proposals.hypothesis:
A deterministic reader working at provision level (the named lõige's passage, own-section pointers, and who points at a selected provision) lands at least 95% of the gold pointer links in the right passage on the in-force national acts, with 0 wrong targets in a 60-link hand-checked sample. The ADR-054 card relations stay under 20% recall on the same links and under 50% on the unreferenced negatives.

Expected gain: in the answer-free search experiment on a new 8-question catalogue written from the gold strata before the run, the provision-level arm (F) finds the deciding phrase in at least 3 more questions than the live cross-reference arm (D), and loses none that D finds in catalogues 1 and 2 (7/9 and 5/6). The cards arm (C) finds at least 1 negative-shaped question that F does not.

Refuted if any of these holds:
- the hand check finds 3 or more wrong targets in 60;
- card relations reach 20% recall on pointer links or 50% on negatives once the repo script recounts my scratch numbers;
- F minus D is under 3 on the new catalogue, or F loses a question D finds.
If the search gain is there but the whole chat (plan, rerank, answer) passes no more of the 8 scenarios than live v3, the mechanism is not switched on (ADR-054 rule: no measurable gain, keep the simpler variant).

proposals.title: M3 step 1: bring the deciding provision in by the act's own structure, measured without the answer model first (ADR-063)
proposals.summary:
Before any new graph work, fix four places where the live search hands the model the wrong passage or none, using only what the acts' own text and the ADR-062 data already say. No model extracts anything, so the relations are right by construction. That answers the roadmap's first M3 question (does using right relations help) for the structural kinds, and it produces the "second, different" hard catalogue S1.0 asks for.

I measured the shapes on the local v47 store (519 acts, all reader v30; 465 in force on 01.10.2026, 9059 passages). No model, no network.

- **Split sections.** 288 of 8282 sections are cut into two or more passages (606 passages, 140 acts). 77 of the 318 cuts fall in the middle of a numbered list. 117 "käesoleva paragrahvi lõike N" references point into another passage of the same section; the reader does not read them, because they carry no § sign.
  - SHS § 59(3) is part 2 of 2 and § 132(7) is part 3 of 3. These are the two catalogue-1 questions cross-references missed.
  - The rest of a split section is 792 tokens at the median and fits 3000 tokens in 598 of 606 cases.
- **References to a subsection.** Search adds the first passage of the referenced section and drops the subsection the reader read. 23 of 472 own-act subsection references land on the wrong passage.
  - SHS § 131, § 132 and § 134 name "§ 133 lõigetes 5 ja 6" (housing costs), which is part 2 of 4. Today the model gets part 1.
  - The § 133(5) list itself is cut after point 3.
- **Application provisions.** All 314 entry-into-force entries of acts in force map to a passage, 58 tokens at the median.
  - 108 acts have a whole-act "rakendatakse" sentence, as Kuusalu § 5(1) does.
  - 38 entries are about single provisions; 19 of them name a section the reader resolves.
  - 12 source cards hide 18 such sentences. SHS shows 1 of 8.
- **Municipal act naming national law.** 364 of 458 municipal acts in force name a provision of one of the six indexed national laws; 1044 of 1052 section references resolve in the version in force.
  - Half of the lists (393 of 784) sit in the preamble as the legal basis. 391 are in section text: 281 passages in 134 acts.
  - The reader returns only a text position for these today, so nothing follows them.
- **Definitions.** 33 passages in 24 acts carry a scoped definition ("käesoleva seaduse tähenduses"); 112 acts have a definitions section. No recorded miss is a definition, so this is measured but not built.

The step turns these into four deterministic rules that share the room live profile v3 already has (4 extra passages, 3000 tokens). They are measured in the answer-free experiment and by replaying stored turns. A rule reaches the chat only if it finds what v3-equivalent search misses and loses nothing.

Paid work is at most three answer-model runs, about 0.14 to 0.40 USD at plan prices. The actual bill has run several times lower (ADR-048). No card extraction is bought.

What this step cannot fix is an exception in another section that nothing names: care-home § 132(7) reached from § 131, and LasteKS § 27¹. Those stay as the test set for hand-checked relations.
proposals.hypothesis:
Arms: A is the base search with no additions, D adds the act's own cross-references as live v3 does, S is D plus the four structure rules in the same room (4 passages, 3000 tokens).

Answer-free, on corpus v47, with a new catalogue "structure-1" of 14 questions written and frozen before any run (10 structure-shaped, 2 that structure cannot reach, 2 controls where nothing should be added):

1. Of the structure-shaped questions where arm D leaves the deciding phrase out of the evidence, arm S brings it in for at least two thirds.
2. S loses no question D found: catalogue 1 stays at 7/9 or better, catalogue 2 at 5/6.
3. S's mean context is at most 800 tokens above D's.
4. At most one in four of S's added passages lies outside the provision the catalogue names as deciding.
5. The two unreachable questions stay missed by S.

Refuted, and v3 stays as it is, when any of these holds:
- D misses fewer than 4 of the 10 structure-shaped questions. Then search does not lose conditions at these shapes and the rules are not needed.
- S finds fewer than two thirds of D's misses.
- S loses a question D found.
- Bound 3 or 4 is exceeded.

Paid check, only after the answer-free result holds: in the whole chat on the same 14 questions, profile v4 states or applies the deciding condition (`must`) on at least 3 more turns than v3 and on none fewer. Otherwise v4 is not shipped.
